How to search, inspect and compare the records

Use the Evidence hub to find a claim, indicator, visual or source-backed record, then inspect the definition, group covered, calculation base, period, geography, method, limitations, source and evidence date. Compare records when similar labels may hide different units or populations. Disagreement, series breaks and missing evidence remain visible rather than being averaged or filled in. The hub is an index for verification; detailed evidence lives in the linked records and comparison view.

Start here: selected evidence records

When was it measured or observed?The official 2026 roster (issue date not stated); 2026 enforcement decisions are separate evidence.
The official 2026 exchange and remittance roster can be counted; whether providers operate now is a separate question
The official 2026 roster of exchange and remittance providers issued by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) lists 100 exchange companies, 231 individual exchange establishments and 111 remittance agents. These are roster entries counted by the roster's own classes: the three class totals are not a count of unique providers, nor a verified count of providers operating now. Because the roster does not state its issue date, CBY-Aden's 2026 decisions (dated January to September 2026) suspending or withdrawing the licences of named entities, or closing their premises, would have to be matched with the roster entity by entity, since a decision may or may not already be reflected in it; that matching has not been done.
Who or what does it apply to? Source-listed exchange companies, individual exchange establishments and remittance agents; entries are counted separately by the three classes used in the official roster.
Does not establish: Adding the three classes does not give a count of unique providers, because no rule for identifying the same entity across classes has been applied. Inclusion in the annual roster is not proof of current operation, branch activity or service availability, including for entities named in 2026 enforcement decisions. Why the numbers differ: the 2025 roster (record CLM-016) listed fewer entries in each of its three classes. The higher 2026 entries cannot be read as new providers entering the market: both rosters count entries by class rather than unique firms, this evidence base has not compared the two rosters entry by entry, and the 2026 roster states no issue date.
Open evidence record Reference CLM-009
When was it measured or observed?Evidence observed from 2014 through 2026, depending on domain, as compared in the current edition of this resource.
Evidence freshness differs by domain
The evidence here is not equally current across domains: several payments/regulatory observations are from 2025–2026, while key representative people-side evidence is older.
Who or what does it apply to? Evidence records across people, payments, providers, reforms and other domains, each with its own observation period and evidence class.
Does not establish: Older evidence is not invalid because of its age, and recent administrative evidence does not measure current financial inclusion across the population.
Open evidence record Reference CLM-014
When was it measured or observed?Decisions dated 1 January to 24 September 2026
Enforcement decisions are events, not a market census
Governor's decisions of the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) dated January to September 2026 record licence withdrawals, suspensions and closures for specific exchange and remittance providers. This record covers selected CBY-Aden Governor's decisions of 2026 concerning exchange and remittance providers (Nos. 1–6, 9–11, 13–15, 17 and 18); other decision numbers are not included and their subjects are not assessed. The official 2026 roster can be counted by class, but these decisions are not subtracted from it to produce a count of providers operating now: each would first have to be matched with the roster entity by entity, and that matching has not been done.
Who or what does it apply to? Only the providers named in the decisions covered here; not the full set of exchange and remittance providers
Does not establish: The 2026 annual roster can be counted by class, but it is not a census of operating providers. Subtracting suspension, withdrawal and closure decisions from the roster does not give a current count of operating providers: the roster does not state its issue date, so each entity a decision names would have to be matched with the roster one by one, without assuming whether the roster already reflects the decision, and that matching has not been done. A provider not named in these decisions is not thereby shown to be active or compliant. The record does not cover 2026 decision numbers other than those listed, and it does not assess their subjects.

When was it measured or observed?World Bank variable pages for the Global Findex 2021 Yemen microdata; Yemen fieldwork 2022–2023.
Raw case shares are not population estimates
World Bank variable pages expose raw sample case counts and percentages for the Yemen Findex file, but explicitly warn that those figures cannot be interpreted as summary statistics of the population of interest.
Who or what does it apply to? Raw respondent cases displayed on World Bank variable pages; these are unweighted sample cases, not the population of Yemen.
Does not establish: The raw, unweighted case percentages shown on the World Bank variable pages are not estimates for Yemen's adult population and are not reported in this resource.

When was it measured or observed?Function-specific people-side evidence: weighted public evidence on financial behaviour centered on 2014, with the latest verified account-ownership value from the Findex 2021 wave and Yemen fieldwork in 2022–2023.
There is no single latest year for all people-side evidence
The people-side evidence here does not have one latest year: account ownership has a latest verified Yemen aggregate in 2022, while weighted public evidence currently available here for account use, saving, borrowing and domestic-remittance behaviour is centered on 2014; latest-wave resilience and barrier values remain unpublished until the required weighted computation is complete. Historical results stay separate from any newer estimate until that computation and its verification are complete.
Who or what does it apply to? People-side evidence by financial function; each function keeps its own survey wave, population base, denominator and publication status.
Does not establish: The 2014 behaviour values do not describe current behaviour, and raw case percentages from the 2021 wave are not a substitute for weighted population estimates.
Open evidence record Reference CLM-031
When was it measured or observed?World Bank public data interfaces as reviewed on 10 September 2026, and earlier documented access
A public interface is not the same thing as the underlying dataset
World Bank public remittance interfaces do not expose Yemen history uniformly. One interface, reviewed on 10 September 2026, showed an older span of years, while other World Bank interfaces and earlier documented retrievals contained later observations. The difference reflects what each interface displays and how its data can be traced; it is not evidence that later underlying data are absent.
Who or what does it apply to? Specific to each source or display interface
Does not establish: The difference does not show that data were deleted or withdrawn, or why any correction was made, and one public interface's observations are not a substitute for another's.
Open evidence record Reference CLM-039
When was it measured or observed?16 July 2026; proposed 18-month IMF Staff-Monitored Program at staff-level agreement stage.
IMF Staff-Monitored Program (SMP) for Yemen: staff-level agreement of July 2026, subject to Management approval
On 16 July 2026, staff of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the Yemeni authorities announced staff-level agreement on key policies and reforms that could underpin a proposed 18-month Staff-Monitored Program (SMP). The IMF stated that the agreement was subject to Management approval and would not result in Board discussion. It is not an IMF financing arrangement. The IMF press release could not be re-opened from this resource on 4 October 2026 (the IMF website refuses automated requests), so the date, the 18-month length and the status above have not been re-read in the original for this edition.
Who or what does it apply to? The staff-level policy agreement between IMF staff and the Yemeni authorities, and the status of the proposed Staff-Monitored Program (SMP); not an Executive Board-approved financing arrangement.
Does not establish: The proposed Staff-Monitored Program (SMP) is not an arrangement approved or endorsed by the Executive Board of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and does not involve IMF financing; the agreement is also not evidence that external-sector statistics have been reconciled.
Open evidence record Reference CLM-049
When was it measured or observed?June 2023 and end-2023 active-borrower observations from separate source chains.
June and end-2023 borrower points are not one continuous series
The roughly 80,800 active-borrower point cited for June 2023 and the 78,686 end-2023 point come through different source chains. They are kept as separate observations until the provider sets and methods behind them are reconciled, and no June-to-year-end decline is calculated from them.
Who or what does it apply to? Active-borrower observations for which it has not yet been shown that the June and year-end points cover the same providers and use the same source method.
Does not establish: The two figures do not establish a decline between June and the end of 2023, monthly values between them, or a continuous series, while the provider sets behind them remain unreconciled.
Open evidence record Reference CLM-057
When was it measured or observed?2024; cumulative/target 2021–2024
The SMEPS financial-services KPI is a programme result, not a national MSME rate
SMEPS's 2024 Annual Report reports that 19% of supported MSMEs accessed financial services in 2024, while the 2021–2024 total reported as achieved is 15% against a 40% programme target. The table does not fully specify the metric-specific assessment base or operational definition of 'accessed financial services'. The KPI can therefore be read only within the programme, subject to that limitation; it is not a national MSME access rate.
Who or what does it apply to? SMEPS-supported MSMEs under the programme KPI
Does not establish: The percentage is not a national rate of access to financial services for micro, small and medium enterprises, a representative survey estimate or a national rate of unique firms, and it does not show that SMEPS caused access.
Open evidence record Reference CLM-060
When was it measured or observed?2022 survey (September 2022); published 2024
Formal firms in the 2022 survey: accounts were common, bank finance for working capital was not
Among formal firms in the 2022 seven-governorate survey, 58.2% (191 of 328) reported a checking or savings account. Their working capital came mainly from internal sources: on average, 69.12% came from internal funds or retained earnings, 16.66% from money lenders, friends or relatives, 10.15% from advance payments by clients, 1.97% from non-bank financial institutions, 1.31% from supplier credit and 0.56% from banks. In a separate question on the financial intermediaries they use, 73.48% of responding formal firms named an exchange store or money exchanger and 24.39% a commercial bank; firms could name more than one, so these are not market shares. The evidence base does not record the number of firms behind the working-capital averages or the intermediary question. Among the 217 informal firms surveyed, 80.18% had no bank account; that sample was drawn from activity and location lists rather than a national register. The formal-firm sample includes micro firms with fewer than five employees, and neither sample represents all Yemeni firms.
Who or what does it apply to? Two separate samples in seven selected governorates: 328 formal enterprises (including micro firms with fewer than five employees) and 217 informal enterprises drawn from activity and location lists. Neither sample represents all Yemeni firms.
Does not establish: The evidence base does not record the number of firms behind the working-capital averages or the intermediary question. An average working-capital share is not a share of firms, and multiple-response percentages are not market shares. Holding an account does not show that a firm uses bank credit. The formal and informal samples use different frames, so they cannot be added together or compared with the 2013 survey. Firms are not people, so these shares are not comparable with the Findex account-ownership rate.

Where is the evidence current — and where is it old?
Evidence dates differ by domain: several payments and regulatory observations date from 2025–2026, while key representative evidence about people is older. Each item is placed by its observation or publication date and by its evidence type: representative survey, administrative record, regulatory material, secondary evidence or unresolved gap. What may explain the number — without pretending to prove it?
This summary starts from one quantitative measure and links it only to contextual mechanisms, policy propositions, research priorities or needs for verification against the original source, where an explicit, documented relationship exists. The links help interpret the number; they do not estimate prevalence, effect size or causality.
Who or what does it apply to? One quantitative measure, linked only to qualitative mechanisms with a documented relationship

When was it measured or observed?28 August 2023 to 23 March 2024
Consumer protection and complaint path: official rules and guidance
Evidence on the consumer-protection and complaint path of the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden): the announcement of the 2023 Financial Consumer Protection Regulatory Instructions (28 August 2023), whose legal text has not been extracted here, and 2024 awareness material and a brochure describing the complaint and escalation steps. Actual complaint handling and redress outcomes are separate questions on which the evidence base holds no evidence.
Who or what does it apply to? Banks and non-bank financial institutions covered by the consumer-protection framework of the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden), as the brochure describes them
Does not establish: The existence of a complaint and redress framework does not establish that consumers use it, that cases are resolved on time, or that redress outcomes are effective.
Open evidence record Reference DS-FCP-ARCH
When was it measured or observed?2024 to 2026
Qualitative evidence register
A structured register of 20 reconciled qualitative evidence items used to interpret mechanisms, institutional conditions and source-specific narratives without turning them into population prevalence or causal estimates.
Who or what does it apply to? Qualitative evidence register
Does not establish: Qualitative evidence can support mechanisms and context, but it does not by itself establish population prevalence, quantified effect size or causality.
Open evidence record Reference DS-QUAL-EVIDENCE
When was it measured or observed?Published 2026; underlying periods vary
OECD, IMF Executive Board and Yemeni authorities: institutional fragility, weak formal access and correspondent banking (qualitative accounts)
The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) links fragmented institutions, supervisory gaps and weak formal access to financial-sector fragility and low trust. On correspondent banking, the OECD writes that the conflict has severely undermined the confidence of several foreign correspondent banks, given perceived risks of money laundering and terrorism financing, isolating the Yemeni banking sector from regional and international financial networks. The IMF's Executive Board, concluding the 2025 Article IV consultation on 31 March 2026, considered the relocation of major banks to Aden an opportunity to strengthen financial stability and integrity, and encouraged enhancing the AML-CFT framework to safeguard correspondent banking relationships. In the statement by the Executive Director for the Republic of Yemen, the authorities say that after the United States designated the Houthis a foreign terrorist organization, all major banks moved their headquarters to Aden to protect correspondent banking relationships and maintain liquidity. The evidence is contextual interpretation, not measured prevalence or a causal effect estimate.
Who or what does it apply to? OECD/EU institutional analysis based on consultations, workshops and sector analysis; the IMF Executive Board's assessment and the Yemeni authorities' statement in the 2025 Article IV consultation.
Does not establish: It cannot establish prevalence, a quantified level of trust or a causal effect size. Its statement on correspondent banks counts no relationships and dates no change: it is the OECD's assessment, not a supervisory record or a measure of de-risking. The IMF passages are the Board's assessment and the authorities' account: neither counts correspondent relationships, and a bank's relocation is not a measure of de-risking or of restored access.
Open evidence record Reference QUAL-001

How many respondents answered each Findex question
Weighted estimates for the 2021 wave have not yet been produced, so no values are shown. When they are published, each will be accompanied by the number of respondents who gave a valid answer, the number of missing or invalid answers, and a note where a question was asked only of a sub-group; these counts describe the sample and are not population estimates.

When was it measured or observed?2014 to 2022; no weighted values yet for some measures in the 2021 wave
Year of the last weighted value for each people-side financial function
The latest weighted evidence differs by financial function: the 2021 Findex wave gives 2022 values for account ownership (11.9%), for saving (21.6%) and borrowing (51.3%) any money and for making or receiving a digital payment (9.3%); the latest weighted value this resource publishes for domestic remittances is from 2014 (18.3% received them), because the World Bank's current series for that measure holds no 2014 value to read it against; and weighted estimates of resilience and of the reasons for not having an account have not yet been calculated for the 2021 wave.
Who or what does it apply to? The latest period with a supported numeric value for each people-side financial function, with account ownership, saving, borrowing, remittances, resilience and barriers kept separate.
Does not establish: It is not a composite inclusion score. There is no single latest year for people-side evidence, and a recent date for one function does not make the evidence for another function current.

Published historical Findex results for Yemen
Weighted Findex values for Yemen from the 2011 and 2014 waves, one value per measure and wave, each with its population base, missing values and publication status, so older measures stay interpretable without being presented as current.
Who or what does it apply to? Adults aged 15 and over in Yemen in the 2011 and 2014 Findex waves; some channel values apply only to adults who sent or received domestic remittances or who have an account.

How recent the people-side evidence is, by financial function

Open evidence record Reference DS-DEMAND-VINTAGE-LENS
When was it measured or observed?Edition of this resource dated 3 October 2026
What kind of evidence is this?
Evidence in this resource falls into distinct types: weighted population measures, administrative records, perception studies, official secondary analysis, recommendations, and the stage a reform or programme has reached. Each type supports different conclusions; the types are not a ranking of truth or a numeric confidence score.
Who or what does it apply to? Evidence records published in this resource only, classified by their nature and by what each can establish
Does not establish: One type of evidence does not stand in for another: a perception is not a population outcome, a recommendation is not implementation, a project milestone is not usage, and an account or transaction is not a unique person. An evidence type is not a probability or certainty score, and the order in which types are presented does not rank them.
Open evidence record Reference VIS-EVIDENCE-CLASS-LADDER

Related measurement priorities

Measurement priorityP0 · Consumer protection / Quality
Consumer experience and redress outcomes
Official material specifies complaint and escalation architecture, including source-defined time windows; actual complaint volumes, resolution times and outcomes are not documented in the available evidence.
Evidence needed: Complaint and redress data from providers and the regulator, plus consumer-side evidence on experience, including fees, disclosure and trust.
Decision it would strengthen: This evidence would allow redress performance and service quality to be assessed rather than inferred from the existence of rules.
